plan.contextChunk: This figure shows a single right triangle drawn in plain black outline with no axes, grid, or shading. The triangle sits on a horizontal base labeled a beneath its midpoint. From the right end of that base a vertical side rises, labeled p on its outer edge. The hypotenuse slants down from the top of the vertical side to the left vertex, labeled h above its middle. A small open square at the lower right vertex marks the right angle between the base and the vertical side, and a single arc at the left vertex marks the acute angle, labeled with the Greek letter theta. The labeling is organized around theta rather than around the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite it, and h is the hypotenuse, so each name states a role rather than a direction. Carrying no numbers at all, the drawing serves as the reference diagram for recovering an unknown acute angle from two known side lengths, the given pair determining which inverse trigonometric relation applies.

interactionPlan.concept: In a right triangle, the side labels adjacent, opposite, and hypotenuse are roles defined relative to the chosen acute angle, and those roles determine which inverse trigonometric function recovers the angle from known side lengths.

horizontal base side labeled a beneath its midpoint
vertical right side labeled p along its outer edge
slanted hypotenuse labeled h above its midpoint
left acute angle arc labeled theta
small open square marking the right angle at the lower right vertex
left vertex where theta is located
lower right vertex joining sides a and p

selected-side highlight overlay for a, p, or h

role callout label reading adjacent, opposite, or hypotenuse

interactions.teaches: A side's name is not just its position on the page: a is adjacent to theta, p is opposite theta, and h is always the hypotenuse because those roles are defined relative to the marked angle.

interactions.label: Angle theta
interactions.teaches: As theta increases, the opposite side grows relative to the adjacent side, so the ratios p/h, a/h, and p/a change in predictable trigonometric ways.

interactions.label: Known side ratio
interactions.teaches: The known pair of side lengths determines the inverse trig relation: p/h points to sine, a/h points to cosine, and p/a points to tangent.

demo_steps.title: Identify the reference angle
demo_steps.narration: The marked angle theta at the left vertex is the reference point for naming the sides. The labels a, p, and h describe each side's role relative to theta, not merely its direction on the page.

demo_steps.title: Click each side role
demo_steps.narration: Click a side to highlight it with theta: a is adjacent because it touches theta, p is opposite because it faces theta, and h is the hypotenuse because it lies across from the right angle.

demo_steps.title: Change theta
demo_steps.narration: Drag theta wider and narrower. The triangle keeps a right angle, but the balance between opposite side p and adjacent side a changes continuously.

demo_steps.title: Choose the inverse trig relation
demo_steps.narration: Enter a known ratio such as p/h, a/h, or p/a. The matching inverse relation is highlighted, showing which formula recovers the unknown angle theta.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Once the sides are named relative to theta, the side pair you know tells you exactly which inverse trig function to use.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Recreate the figure as a clean black-outline right triangle with no axes, grid, numbers, or shading. Place the base horizontally from left to right, the vertical side rising at the right end, and the hypotenuse slanting upward from the left vertex to the top of the vertical side. Put the right-angle square at the lower right corner and the theta arc at the left vertex. Keep labels in simple italic math style: a below the base, p just outside the vertical side, h above the hypotenuse, and theta beside the left angle arc. For the slider, hold the hypotenuse length visually constant while theta changes, so a shortens and p lengthens as theta increases. Use a warm highlight color for the selected side and theta arc, and show the inverse trig callout near the triangle without cluttering the original minimal diagram.

authoredContext:
Given two sides of a right triangle like the one shown in the figure, find an angle.

An illustration of a right triangle with an angle theta. Adjacent to theta is the side a, opposite theta is the side p, and the hypoteneuse is side h.
